conventions.convention: The complete-data density is supplied as one jointly measurable function, normalized on every parameter fibre. Joint measurability is not inferred from separate likelihood versions.

Latent densities and observed log likelihoods are defined only on fibres with positive finite observed marginal. Q is assigned only when its integral is finite; absolute log-integrability is required for admissibility.

KL runs from the current latent law to the candidate latent law. Admissibility requires current-to-candidate absolute continuity and finite directional KL. AC is assumed for the Radon–Nikodym branch; failure of absolute continuity gives infinite KL without selecting a derivative.

Exact mode selects an attained Q maximizer over an admissible candidate set containing the current iterate. Generalized mode requires only nondecreasing Q. Iteration starts at t=0; unavailable updates stop without appending a failed candidate.
Use log 0 = −∞ and assign q_t times absolute log density the value zero wherever q_t=0. An extended diagnostic integral equal to −∞ is not a value of the algorithm's finite-valued Q.

load_bearing.statement: Defines EM on supplied jointly measurable normalized complete-data densities, with positive finite marginal fibres, finite log-integrable Q, support-compatible finite-KL candidates, attained exact updates or Q-nondecreasing generalized updates, and explicit stopping on unavailable updates.

Assume AC, a jointly measurable normalized complete-data density, fixed observed data, positive finite current and candidate marginals, current-to-candidate latent absolute continuity, absolute integrability of both complete-data log densities under the current latent law, and finite directional KL. Then ℓ_x(θ)−ℓ_x(θ_t)=Q(θ|θ_t)−Q(θ_t|θ_t)+D(q_t μ||q_θ^x μ). Consequently an admissible Q-nondecreasing update does not decrease ℓ_x; an attained exact maximizer over an admissible set containing θ_t has this property.

Assume AC and the model, fibre, support, integrability, and finite-KL hypotheses of the EM ascent theorem. An admissible candidate with Q(θ_{t+1}|θ_t)≥Q(θ_t|θ_t) satisfies ℓ_x(θ_{t+1})≥ℓ_x(θ_t). The Q maximizer need not be attained.
